item.title: Katy Perry faces heat for space trip while attending Davos climate talks: 'Burned 498 tons of fuel'
item.description: Katy Perry, renowned pop sensation, is under fire for her recent venture into space tourism, with critics pointing to contradictions in her environmental commitment. Although her sub-orbital adventure was hailed as a groundbreaking achievement for women, it also raised eyebrows due to the substantial carbon footprint associated with such flights.

item.title: Row over Trump’s hand bruise in Davos and ‘missing medical records’: ‘Two years of Biden’s health…’
item.description: During a high-profile ceremony at Davos, President Trump's visibly bruised hand ignited fresh discussions about his health transparency. The White House quickly explained the marks were due to a minor mishap with a table and that daily aspirin intake, which he increased for blood thinning, could lead to more bruising.

item.title: Missouri man sells a car to eight people on Facebook, then steals it back within 24 hours every time
item.description: A Kansas City man faces 14 felony counts for allegedly running a Facebook Marketplace scam, selling vehicles to multiple buyers and then stealing them back. Prosecutors say Mamadou Diallo used forged paperwork, convincing victims to pay thousands before the cars disappeared. The scheme reportedly occurred across at least eight sales in May and June 2025.

item.title: Is Europe ready to boycott the 2026 FIFA World Cup over Trump’s threats to Greenland?
item.description: Five months before kickoff, the 2026 World Cup is being pulled into geopolitics, as Donald Trump’s rhetoric over Greenland strains US–Europe relations. While no European federation has committed to a boycott, politicians and football officials are openly debating withdrawal, raising the once-unthinkable prospect of a politically fractured World Cup.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Marvel Rivals streamer Kingsman265 surges on Twitch after being dropped from $40K event
item.description: A Marvel Rivals streamer named Kingsman265 saw a huge surge in Twitch followers and subscribers. This happened after he was removed from a tournament. His former teammates had an argument with him. Many viewers supported Kingsman265. He received over three thousand dollars in donations. The game developers also sent him in-game credits. This controversy unexpectedly boosted his career.

item.title: Piece or peace? Elon Musk takes a jab at Donald Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ — watch
item.description: Elon Musk poked fun at Donald Trump's "Board of Peace," questioning if it was about "piece" of territory. Trump launched the board in Davos as part of his plan to end the Gaza war, with several nations joining. However, France and Slovenia declined, citing conflicts with international law and order.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Sorry I killed your daughter, hope you’re still a fan’: Shri Thanedar jibes at Trump over remarks on Renee Good’s death
item.description: In a passionate denunciation, Congressman Shri Thanedar has taken a stand against President Trump's controversial comments regarding the tragic death of Renee Nicole Good at the hands of an ICE agent. Instead of expressing sympathy, Trump chose to highlight the deceased's father's political views, prompting Thanedar to describe the President as a 'deranged sociopath.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Not just vandalism’: Statue damaged at Hindu temple in US, investigation under way
item.description: A sacred guardian statue at the Sri Venkateswara Temple in Cary, North Carolina, was vandalized on January 18. Hindu advocacy groups are condemning the act as an attack on their community, urging a thorough investigation into potential bias. Police are reviewing surveillance footage, and restoration efforts are underway, with no arrests made yet.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: From arrest to deportation: Mahmoud Khalil’s journey from pro-Palestinian activist to anti-Israel spokesperson
item.description: In a dramatic turn of events, Mahmoud Khalil, an activist championing Palestinian rights and a one-time Columbia University student, finds himself on the brink of deportation from the United States. After enduring more than 100 days in detention, he was initially released by a federal judge.

item.title: FBI arrests activist and school board member over St. Paul church ICE protest — who are Nekima Levy Armstrong and Chauntyll Louisa Allen?
item.description: Two activists, Nekima Levy Armstrong and St. Paul School Board member Chauntyll Louisa Allen, were arrested following a protest at Cities Church. The demonstration, which disrupted a service where an ICE official is a pastor, was in response to the fatal shooting of Renee Good by an ICE agent.

item.title: Socialist vs Billionaire: Why Zohran Mamdani's relationship with NYPD chief is key for New York
item.description: Mamdani, 34, rode a wave of anti-establishment anger to City Hall, campaigning on taxing the rich, rethinking policing and shifting resources towards housing and mental health. Tisch, 44, is the scion of one of New York’s wealthiest families and a firm believer in proactive policing. She was appointed commissioner in 2024 and quickly earned plaudits from corporate leaders for driving down crime.

item.title: UAE new child digital safety law puts parents at risk of fines up to AED 1 million
item.description: The UAE has enacted a new Child Digital Safety Law, holding parents legally accountable for their children's online activities. Effective January 1, 2026, the law mandates "Digital Due Diligence," requiring guardians to ensure age-appropriate platform use and prevent data sharing. Neglect can result in fines ranging from AED 5,000 to AED 100,000, with potential for mandatory digital rehabilitation courses.
